method: Legacy knockout+top-two versus adaptive policies in the same candidate executable. 50 seeded runs per scenario and policy; 12 entrants; 320 new completed games plus shared sparse initial draws. Admission adds four entrants at game 80. Game completions are asynchronous, with capacity 8 -> 2 -> 8; reduced capacity retains workers 0 and 2. Both policies use the corrected rematch start rule. Scores use latent strengths, color advantage, draws; correlated case adds a +/-0.65 log-odds opening effect shared by paired legs. Held-out seed range 50..99, selected by SCHEDULER_SEED_START=50. No learning-policy changes were made after inspecting these seeds; the subsequent aborted-slot migration fix does not affect these simulations.
limits: Synthetic recovery of unordered top-five membership, not measured real-engine strength, wall-clock throughput, or error calibration. Baseline is the legacy policy compiled in the candidate, not a separately built parent binary. These seeds were not used for policy selection, but the scenarios and latent strengths are the same as development. This is a held-out random-outcome check, not validation across a broad range of game-strength models. Approximate paired normal intervals describe variability across 50 run-level recovery differences; no multiple-comparison correction. Zero false-inactivation events is not a guarantee.

environment.profile: cargo --release; in-process synthetic game outcomes; no engine searches
